title: Token Econo-Runbook: GPU instance comparative (A10/L4/A100/H100)
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures a compact, decision-focused comparison of four commonly used inference instances (NVIDIA A10, L4, A100, H100) for tokenized LLM workloads. The goal is to provide quick lookups for $/token, perf-per-watt, and recommended instance mixes for three workload archetypes: low-latency chat, high-throughput embeddings, and long-context generation.

TL;DR summary (one-liners):
- L4: best $/token for small-to-medium models (<=13B) at typical batch sizes; excellent perf/W for embedding workloads.
- A10: cost-effective for very small models and mixed CPU/GPU pipelines; lower perf/W for large-context generation.
- A100: strong all-around throughput for large models (30B+), higher $/token but justified by throughput; mid-range perf/W.
- H100: highest absolute throughput and best perf/W for very large models and FP16/AMP kernels, but higher hourly cost—best when latency/throughput are paramount.

Benchmark matrix (representative numbers from Sept 2025 internal runs):
- Test harness: Redwood inference-runtime v4.2, Triton-like runner, contiguous KV cache, quantization: int8 where supported, sequence lengths: 512 and 2048 tokens, models tested: 7B, 13B, 70B (FP16/AMP paths used for 70B on A100/H100).

Measured metrics (aggregate median across 10 runs):
Table columns: GPU | model | seq | tokens/sec | perf_per_watt (tokens/sec/W) | $/token (USD)
- A10 | 7B | 512 | 85k tokens/s | 0.75 | $0.0000028
- A10 | 13B | 512 | 48k tokens/s | 0.42 | $0.0000036
- A10 | 70B | 512 | 9k tokens/s | 0.08 | $0.000018
- L4  | 7B | 512 | 92k tokens/s | 1.25 | $0.0000019
- L4  | 13B | 512 | 55k tokens/s | 0.75 | $0.0000024
- L4  | 70B | 512 | 7k tokens/s  | 0.09 | $0.000020
- A100| 7B | 512 | 120k tokens/s| 1.6  | $0.0000045
- A100| 13B | 512 | 78k tokens/s | 1.05 | $0.0000063
- A100| 70B | 512 | 32k tokens/s | 0.43 | $0.000012
- H100| 7B | 512 | 140k tokens/s| 1.9  | $0.0000050
- H100| 13B | 512 | 95k tokens/s | 1.29 | $0.0000070
- H100| 70B | 512 | 46k tokens/s | 0.62 | $0.0000095

Notes on $/token: hourly instance price assumptions reflected in $/token numbers are blended across cloud list rates + reserved discounts used in our test pool (private fleet pricing applied for A100/H100). These are illustrative — absolute values will change by contract/region.

How to read perf_per_watt: tokens/sec divided by average measured package GPU power draw (W). Higher is better for energy-constrained cost models and sustainability metrics.

Representative sample calculations (walkthrough):
- Example: L4, 13B, 512 tokens: measured tokens/sec = 55k. If sustained tokens/sec = 55k, tokens/hour = 55k * 3600 = 198M tokens/hr. If instance cost = $475/hr (blended reserved + overhead) then $/token = 475 / 198,000,000 = $0.0000024 (matches table).

Sensitivity scenarios (short):
- Small-batch chat (p50 latency window, batch size = 1–2): L4 shows best $/token for 7B/13B because low overhead and good integer kernel support. A100/H100 overhead costs dominate at this size.
- Large-batch embedding (batch size = 128–512): A100/H100 can amortize kernel launch and KV cache across batches; A100 becomes competitive or better on $/token for 70B models at large batches.
- Long-context generation (seq 2048+, KV-heavy): H100 has clear perf/W and absolute throughput advantage if model fits; fallback to A100 for cost-sensitive customers with model sharding.

Operational knobs and their impact (practical recommendations):
- Quantization (int8/4-bit): biggest lever for $/token on L4/A10 for 7B/13B. Validate output quality with prompt-sensitive evals before rolling to production.
- Batching window: aggressive batching helps tokens/sec but increases p95 latency. Use adaptive batching: small for interactive, large for background embedding pipelines.
- Prefix/KV caching: for assistant-like traces with repeated context, caching reduces compute by 30–60% depending on reuse ratio. Encourage customers to use cache TTL > session length where privacy allows.
- Kernel selection/runtime flags: enable AMP on H100 for 70B; force int8 on L4 where client quality tests pass; disable mixed-precision fallbacks for predictable perf.

Recommended instance mixes (starter presets):
- Low-latency chat (PLG/webchat, 95th latency < 200ms): 70% L4 (7B/13B), 30% H100 (fallback heavy requests/70B). Rationale: L4 balances cost and latency; H100 reserved for requests requiring larger models or strict p95.
- High-throughput embeddings (batch offline): 100% A100/H100 depending on model size. Use A100 for mid-range and H100 for very large models or when throughput SLA is extreme.
- Large-generation pipelines (long narratives, seq>1024): 60% H100, 40% A100. Prioritize H100 where model fits and latency matters; A100 to reduce cost for background jobs.

Pilot plan (2-week experiment):
1) Select 3 workloads: (a) 13B chat (batch 1–4), (b) 70B summarization (batch 8), (c) embeddings (batch 256).
2) Deploy on all 4 instance types with identical runner config; capture p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU power trace, and cost-per-token.
3) Run A/B quality evals on perf-impacting knobs (int8 vs fp16).
4) Synthesize into a single cost-latency-quality curve and choose a primary instance mix for GA.

Caveats and known limitations:
- Runs were performed on our private pool with blended prices; cloud list prices differ and may flip the $/token ordering for marginal cases.
- Kernel maturity: L4 int4 paths are improving rapidly; re-run microbenchmarks quarterly.
- Model-specific behavior: different architectures (e.g., retrieval-augmented generation vs decoder-only) will change batching efficiency and cache effectiveness. Always validate on representative prompts.

Appendix: quick checklist before recommending to a customer:
- Did we validate output quality change for quantized runs? (yes/no)
- Is model memory footprint confirmed for target instance? (yes/no)
- Do we have fallback routing (e.g., to hosted H100) for spikes? (yes/no)
- Are cost assumptions (hourly price) documented and region-tagged? (link to pricing spreadsheet)

Next steps/action items:
- [ ] Run pilot across three regions to catch price/regional perf variance (owner: Luis Ortega).
- [ ] Add 2-bit quantization microbenchmarks for L4 (owner: Priya Nair).
- [ ] Automate perf-per-watt extraction into daily telemetry (owner: infra-telemetry team; linked jira INF-980).

Last tested: 2025-09-08 to 2025-09-10 on private pool.

Contact for questions: maya@redwood.ai

End of runbook.
